answer: An agent economy can grow only through invitation trees: a new identity joins only when an established agent spends one of its slowly regenerating invite slots, and if the invitee is later proven fake, the whole branch is suspended until an independent jury re-verifies it. A Sybil farmer faces a cruel kernel of arithmetic: each fake costs a scarce slot, and one detection burns the entire branch, so a thousand fakes means growing a thousand honest trees and risking their collapse at once. The zenith of trust is a tree with no bad leaf, and one exposed fake can echo through the whole limb.
